title.narrative: PRO-WOMEN - Fortalecimiento de los derechos y la autonomia de las mujeres rurales

description.narrative: This project, which is being implemented in the municipalities of Lepaera and Las Flores Lempira, has as its central objective the building of relationships based on equality and respect that foster more inclusive and sustainable communities. The project is based on gender justice and participation in local organisations, particularly those involved in water management, and seeks to strengthen the knowledge and exercise of the rights of women who are victims of violence, promoting their economic empowerment as a means of protection and autonomy, and their active leadership in water governance. Outcome 1 (Rights and Autonomy): This focuses on empowering women through knowledge-building, with an emphasis on ESCR (Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights), as well as on women’s socio-emotional recovery through the creation of self-help groups, the development of legal skills, and the establishment of an alert system (a community protection network based on trust and rapid response via telephone, established as a control message; for example: creation of a group chat/WhatsApp where a specific emoji (e.g. a red dot or a flower) or a missed call is sent) for contact between participants) for mutual support. In parallel, work is being done to deconstruct masculine norms with community leaders to ensure violence-free environments, supported by a gender and environmental awareness campaign. • Outcome 2 (Women’s Economic Empowerment): Promotes financial independence as a means of protection against gender-based violence, through a programme of technical and business training. The initiative stands out for promoting green economy initiatives (recycling, organic production, renewable energy), providing female entrepreneurs with supplies and mentoring to help them market their products, as well as linking them to Savings and Credit Groups (GACs) to ensure their financial sustainability. Outcome 3 (Safe Participation of Women in Community Forums): This component strengthens the capacity of community water structures to transform local governance into an equitable and protective space. Through an assessment of gender barriers, the project identifies and removes obstacles that hinder women’s leadership, implementing training programmes on the Human Right to Water with a focus on climate resilience. At the heart of this outcome is the creation of safe participation protocols, ensuring that women’s empowerment translates into real and protected influence within the Water Boards. Finally, technical evidence is generated through research on resilience and rights, linking environmental sustainability with gender justice.
